scope: Credential screening and sanitizer behavior, binary chunking, false negatives, multi-chunk leakage and false positives: src/security.ts (Redactor.text/value/contains, redactorFor, excerptText), src/files.ts (artifact chunking, overlap pad screen, logs), src/mcp.ts (get_worker_artifact resource link, worker-artifact template), src/settings/inspect.ts + src/settings/load.ts (redactedSettings, redact, collectSecrets, credential context), src/serve-command.ts (commandRedactor), src/coordinator.ts, src/http.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/config.ts

findings.title: Artifact chunk credential screen is defeated by a credential longer than the overlap pad; credential bytes are returned to the caller
findings.evidence: readArtifact derives the overlap from only two of the four secret sources in redactorFor: pad = Math.max(4096, config.SWARMFORGE_MODEL_API_KEY.length, config.FREESTYLE_API_TOKEN.length) (src/files.ts:94-98), while the screen at src/files.ts:103 is an exact whole-secret substring match over the decoded window (Redactor.contains, src/security.ts:38-41) against the four-source set from redactorFor (src/security.ts:44-49: FREESTYLE_API_TOKEN, SWARMFORGE_MODEL_API_KEY, SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN, and every worker's server_password). SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN is the only omitted source with no schema length ceiling (src/config.ts:81, z.string().min(24).optional()). With start = max(0, offset - pad) and window length + 2*pad, any read at offset > pad truncates such a credential at the window's LEFT edge, the exact match fails, no exception is thrown, and src/files.ts:107 returns the portion inside the caller's range: up to secretLength - 4097 contiguous credential bytes. The RIGHT edge is sound because the window extends pad past the chunk end (verified). Trigger: a worker artifact larger than one chunk holds the configured SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN and the lead walks next_offset; offset=0 is refused, offset=32768 starts its window at 28672 and returns 904 bytes of the credential.
findings.reproduction: Reproduced. Disposable detached worktree at /tmp/rev-24 (git rev-parse HEAD = target d428e0f730ed5649485732e95d39c32f5d6a8895), official Bun 1.4.2 at /tmp/bun142, bun install --frozen-lockfile exit 0. Probe at /tmp/probe/probe.ts (outside the source checkout) uses a fake WorkerProvider with a byte-range readFile plus a real Coordinator/Store/WorkerFiles, sets SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN to a synthetic 5000-character placeholder (schema-legal, min 24, no max; the two tokens folded into pad left short), stores a 60000-byte artifact with the token at absolute bytes [0,5000), then calls readArtifact(id, 'blob.bin', 4196, 32768). Observed: pad=4096, provider window start=100 len=40960 (token truncated to its last 4900 bytes), no exception, 804 contiguous credential bytes returned whose leading characters match the token prefix. Controls in the same run that PASSED, isolating the defect to the left edge: short secret inside the chunk -> refused; the same 5000-character token at absolute byte 5000 -> refused; the token straddling the right window edge -> refused; junk high bytes (c3 28 e0 80 80 fe ff) before an ASCII secret -> still detected (rules out UTF-8 decode consumption as an alternative cause). Also verified server_password is a fixed 72 chars (src/store.ts:96, two randomUUIDs), so that omission is latent rather than exploitable.
findings.recommendation: Derive the overlap from the live secret set so the screen and the secret set cannot drift: in readArtifact, const secrets = redactorFor(this.c).secrets().filter(Boolean); const pad = Math.max(4096, ...secrets.map((s) => Buffer.byteLength(s))); then start = Math.max(0, offset - pad). Use Buffer.byteLength rather than String.length so the pad is in bytes, matching the byte offsets used by readFile and contains. Consider screening in latin1 (byte-preserving) or scanning the raw bytes so no decode step can drop a partial match. Add a regression test that reads a second/third chunk of an artifact holding a SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN longer than the pad with the credential straddling offset - pad; the existing tests/api.test.ts:104-127 only reads offset 0 with 12-byte secrets, which cannot observe the boundary.
findings.confidence: high on mechanism (reproduced end-to-end through the real readArtifact); medium on real-world likelihood because it requires a schema-legal but atypical SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN above 4096 bytes - documented as 'minimum 24 characters' with no documented maximum

tests.command: cd /tmp/rev-24 && /tmp/bun142/bun-linux-x64/bun test tests/api.test.ts tests/excerpt.test.ts tests/inspect.test.ts -> exit 0, 20 pass, 0 fail, 92 expect(); /tmp/bun142/bun-linux-x64/bun test tests/commands.test.ts tests/settings.test.ts -> exit 0, 71 pass, 0 fail, 627 expect(); /tmp/bun142/bun-linux-x64/bun run /tmp/probe/probe.ts -> exit 1, 1 failure (probe A1, the reproduced MEDIUM leak), 8 controls passed
tests.summary: Targeted in-scope suites only: 91 tests pass, 0 fail, across api/excerpt/inspect/commands/settings. The reviewer's own probe exits 1 solely because assertion A1 (no credential bytes returned) fails, which is the reproduced MEDIUM finding. Setup: bun install --frozen-lockfile exit 0 in the disposable checkout, lockfile unmodified. Snapshot Bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2, so official Bun 1.4.2 was unpacked at /tmp/bun142 and the lockfile was never rewritten. Full suite deliberately not run (whole-suite reviewer's job). No real cloud/model provider, VM, network service or real credential was used; all providers are local fakes and all secrets are synthetic placeholders.

limitations: Full suite not run; git-handoff, lifecycle, safety, packaging, serve, wait, http, core, adapters, cli, overview, restart, process-lock, session-status, smoke and token-idle were not executed.
Nothing compiled or packaged (packaging scope); no tsc or biome run.

The MEDIUM finding was reproduced against a fake provider whose readFile honors the documented byte-range contract; src/providers/freestyle.ts:302-304 forwards {offset, length} to the SDK fs.readFile, asserted from code only, not exercised against the real Freestyle API per the no-real-infrastructure constraint.

redactedSettings and collectSecrets were assessed by code reading plus the passing settings/inspect suites; no adversarial TOML/env fuzzing, so rarer false negatives there (for example a credential inside a TOML inline table echoed verbatim by a parse error) remain unverified hypotheses rather than findings.

Redactor.text's base64 variant covers only a contiguous whole-secret encoding; a line-wrapped (PEM-style) base64 credential would not be matched. Treated as an unverified design limitation, not a finding, since no in-scope code path emits wrapped base64 of a configured secret.

The pad defect was also observed at the Redactor.contains level for a short non-ASCII secret truncated by one byte at a window edge; folded into the same finding as evidence of the window invariant rather than scored separately, since the right-edge cut lies outside the returned range.
No node_modules or lockfile change was made to /workspace/repo; the disposable worktree /tmp/rev-24 was removed after the review.
